extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: A bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding, comprising 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li
extraction.publisher: Tsinghua University, Zhipu.AI, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data is extracted from existing public datasets and manually curated for MultiFieldQA from various sources. Extraction strategies include random sampling to maintain a natural length distribution and uniform sampling based on length to study capabilities across varying context lengths.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public datasets (NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, DuReader, GovReport, QMSum, MultiNews, VCSUM, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, LSHT, LCC, RepoBench-P), Wikipedia, C4 Dataset, WuDaoCorpora, Chinese Judgements Online, Chinese Government Websites, and Github.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For multi-doc QA, supporting passages are included and distracting passages are added until a maximum length is reached, then randomly ordered. For few-shot learning, examples are randomly sampled from the training set and concatenated. For synthetic tasks, passages are repeated, shuffled, or summarized.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All 21 datasets are standardized into a unified format (Input, Context, Answer). Data is extracted from the test sets of public datasets to avoid test leakage. Passages in TriviaQA with less than 1,000 words were filtered to be examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For MultiFieldQA, annotators proposed one question and a groundtruth answer for each document. Questions were required to be clear with definitive, relatively short answers, and the distribution of evidence paragraphs was kept random throughout the article. Questions included varied types such as information-extracting, summarizing, and multi-hop reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-validation among annotators shows a 100% accuracy rate of the annotated answers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Ph.D. students with extensive research experience in the field of NLP.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: During annotation, the placement of evidence was kept fairly random to avoid biases that might occur if answer-related statements are frequently found at the beginning or the end of documents.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Potentially unreliable automatic metrics (ROUGE-L, F1 may not accurately reflect response quality, especially for longer responses) and coupling with instruction-following capabilities (performance is coupled with the models' instruction-following capabilities).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating long context understanding capabilities of large language models (LLMs) across tasks like single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion.
